overview: Gugustus's Disabler is a configurable packet killer and anti-cheat bypass suite. Each BooleanValue setting toggles a separate behavior: cancelling specific serverbound packets (keepalive, ping, entity action, abilities, transactions), spoofing the client brand to BLC, faking abilities for RoyalPixels, or running the HAC/AAC5 teleport spam exploits. The ping-spoof mode buffers keepalives and releases them late from a render-3D tick, and the NoFlag mode cancels S08 teleports it considers small enough to eat silently.

sections.p: A single packet-send event handler (onEventSendPacket) dispatches on packet type, with one boolean flag per bypass. State is kept in a keepalive buffer list and a 'disabling' flag that the UniversoCraft mode toggles across respawn/attack/movement events. Settings use the Gugustus BooleanValue/DoubleValue framework, which stores the value by an integer id, not the field name.

Ping spoofing without a timer: intercept C00 keepalives, store them with a release timestamp (now + delay + 0-200ms jitter), cancel the originals, then flush them from onEventRender3D via addToSendQueueDirect so the server sees a delayed echo and measures inflated ping. The HAC mode sends a C06 position 11 blocks below every 10 ticks; AAC5 sends an extreme y-offset (1.0E159) pair; both exploit server-side movement validation gaps. NoFlag cancels S08 teleports within 8 blocks and re-sends the position itself as C06, keeping the server's view while suppressing the client-side snap.

The modes are named after the anticheats they target (HAC, AAC5, NCPTimerSemi) and the servers they were built for (RoyalPixels, UniversoCraft, Minemen). The BLC spoof rewrites the MC|Brand payload to 'blc' so server-side brand checks classify the client as Badlion. The UniversoCraft transaction-uid flip (Short.MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE on even/odd ticks under 350 ticks) targets a specific transaction-validation quirk on that network.

annotations.text: Package declaration: this class lives in Gugustus's misc module package alongside other non-combat utilities.
Standard imports: AWT Color for the module color, ArrayList for the keepalive buffer.

Client-framework imports: Unpooled for crafting the spoofed brand payload, the event classes (wildcard), module base classes, settings framework, PlayerUtil/RandomUtil helpers, and the custom CustomC00PacketKeepAlive type that carries a release timestamp alongside the keepalive key.

Event API and Minecraft imports: EventTarget annotation marks event handlers; Packet/PacketBuffer for the C17 rewrite; the serverbound play packet wildcard (all C0x classes); S02PacketChat and S08PacketPlayerPosLook for receive-side handling; C01PacketPing for the status ping cancel.
Class declaration: Disabler extends Module, the client's module base. Every module in Gugustus follows this pattern (constructor registers name/color/category).
The keepalive buffer: packets are parked here when ping-spoofing instead of being sent, then flushed later. CustomC00PacketKeepAlive pairs the keepalive key with an absolute release timestamp.
A counter field that is never incremented anywhere in this file; dead code left over from an earlier iteration.
PingSpoof toggle: when enabled, outgoing C00 keepalives are intercepted and delayed (see onEventSendPacket and onEventRender3D).
RoyalPixels toggle: sends a fake C13 abilities packet claiming flying is allowed (see onEventUpdate).
MinemenStrafe toggle: drops every third C0F transaction, tuned for the Minemen network's anticheat.
UniversoCraft toggle: the transaction-uid flip exploit described in onEventSendPacket.
Spectate toggle: on every C03 movement packet, also sends C18PacketSpectate for the player's own UUID, a spectator-mode desync trick.
keepAlive toggle: blanket-cancels every C00 keepalive (no delay, no echo).
ping toggle: blanket-cancels status C01PacketPing packets.
entityAction toggle: blanket-cancels C0B entity actions (sprint/sneak states).
playerAbilities toggle: blanket-cancels C13 abilities packets, stopping the server from learning about client-side ability changes.
confirmTransaction toggle: blanket-cancels C0F confirmations, breaking the server's inventory-transaction tracking.
NCPTimerSemi toggle: a NoCheatPlus timer bypass that nudges the player down 0.017 blocks and sets motionY to 0.019 every tick (see onEventUpdate).
Commented-out toggles (VulcanStrafe, VulcanCombat, SpamSprint): disabled during development, kept as reference.
HAC toggle: the 11-block C06 teleport spam targeting the HAC anticheat (see onEventUpdate).
NoSprint toggle: cancels START_SPRINTING entity actions so the server never sees the player sprint (see onEventSendPacket).
BLC-Spoof toggle: rewrites the MC|Brand custom payload to 'blc' so the server fingerprints the client as Badlion (see onEventSendPacket).
AAC5 toggle: the extreme 1.0E159 y-offset position pair targeting AAC version 5 (see onEventUpdate).
NoFlag toggle: the S08 teleport eater that re-sends the position itself (see onRecv).
Debug toggle: prints 'sex' to chat when the NoFlag teleport eat fires, for verifying the bypass live.
Delay setting (ms) used by ping spoofing: how long keepalives are held before release; range 1-4000ms, default 1000ms.
DisableOnWorld toggle: auto-disables the module when the world changes (see onWorld).
EventTarget annotation: registers onWorld as an event listener on the client's event bus.

World-change handler: if DisableOnWorld is on, the module turns itself off when a new world loads. This avoids leaving cancellation modes active across a respawn/join where they would cause a disconnect.
The 'disabling' state flag used by the UniversoCraft mode to know when to corrupt transactions.
Constructor: registers the module with the name 'Disabler', a slate-blue color, and the MISC category.
onEnable: clears the keepalive buffer so no stale parked packets survive from a previous session.
onDisable: clears the keepalive buffer again. Parked keepalives are dropped rather than flushed, so disabling mid-bypass does not dump a burst of stale echoes.
EventTarget onEventUpdate: runs every client tick (EventUpdate fires on each world tick while in game).

NCPTimerSemi: teleports the player 0.017 blocks down and sets motionY to 0.019. The tiny repeated position jitter desynchronizes NoCheatPlus's timer/position averaging while the upward motion cancels the downward drift visually.

HAC mode: every 10 ticks, sends a C06 position-look 11 blocks below the player with onGround=true. The server-side movement validator on HAC accepts the 11-block drop as legitimate fall damage territory instead of flagging teleport, keeping the player's client-side position authoritative.

AAC5 mode: sends two C06 packets with a y-offset of 1.0E159 (essentially negative infinity) and then the real position. The absurd first value poisons AAC5's y-motion accumulator before the legitimate position lands, so the check sees an impossible jump and stops trusting the stream. Skipped on integrated servers (singleplayer).

RoyalPixels mode: constructs a fresh C13 abilities packet, sets both allowFlying and flying, and sends it. This claims creative-flight capability on a server that normally disables flying, enabling flight on networks that trust the client's abilities packet.
EventTarget onEventRender3D: fires every render frame in 3D, a higher-frequency cadence than the tick loop. Used here as the keepalive flush clock.

Ping spoof flush: iterates the parked keepalives; any whose release time has passed is sent directly (addToSendQueueDirect bypasses the event bus, so the module does not re-intercept its own echo), then removed. The server therefore receives each keepalive late by delay+0-200ms and folds that latency into the player's ping.
EventTarget onEventSendPacket: the main interception point. Fires for every serverbound packet before it hits the network; the module can cancel or replace the packet.
Extracts the raw packet object from the event.

UniversoCraft mode: a state machine over the packet stream. A respawn (S07) sets 'disabling'; a use-entity attack (C02) clears it; movement (C03) within the first 10 ticks sets it. While 'disabling' and under 350 ticks, every C0F transaction has its uid flipped to Short.MIN_VALUE or Short.MAX_VALUE depending on tick parity, corrupting the server's transaction bookkeeping just enough to confuse the anticheat without desyncing the inventory.
NoSprint mode: cancels START_SPRINTING entity-action packets, so the server believes the player never sprints (useful for bypasses that need the server to think movement is walk-speed).

PingSpoof intercept: when a C00 keepalive is about to be sent, its key is wrapped in a CustomC00PacketKeepAlive with release time = now + delay + 0-200ms random jitter, added to the buffer, and the original packet is cancelled. The delayed re-send happens in onEventRender3D.
MinemenStrafe mode: cancels every third C0F transaction (ticksExisted % 3 == 0), tuned to Minemen's transaction-based anticheat which tolerates occasional drops.

Generic keepalive kill switch: when the keepAlive toggle is on, all C00 packets are cancelled outright, with no echo. The server stops getting keepalives; safe only on servers without a keepalive timeout.
Status ping kill switch: cancels C01PacketPing, freezing the server-side ping display.
Entity action kill switch: cancels all C0B packets so the server never sees sprint/sneak state changes.
Abilities kill switch: cancels C13 packets so client-side ability changes are never reported.
Transaction kill switch: cancels all C0F confirmations, breaking inventory-transaction tracking entirely.

Spectate mode: whenever the client sends a C03 movement packet, also injects C18PacketSpectate for the player's own UUID. Spectating yourself desynchronizes the server's camera entity from the player entity, which some anticheats mis-handle.
BLC-Spoof mode: intercepts C17 custom payloads on the MC|Brand channel and replaces them with a fresh payload whose string is 'blc', so server-side brand checks fingerprint the client as Badlion.
EventTarget onRecv: fires for every packet received from the server; used by the NoFlag teleport eater.

NoFlag mode: when an S08 teleport arrives after tick 20, computes the Euclidean distance between the teleport target and the current position. If within 8 blocks, the teleport is cancelled and the position is re-sent as a C06 with onGround=true (addToSendQueueDirect avoids re-triggering the receive path). The client keeps its position, the server gets the position anyway, and the anticheat's teleport confirmation sees a clean movement instead of a snap. The debug toggle prints 'sex' when this fires.
Closing brace of the class.
